messages:
Tara V: Heads-up — customers on the ws endpoint are seeing mid-stream stalls but our dashboard alerting insists there are no socket closes. This looks like a ping/pong mismatch between edge and origin. Anyone saw this pattern after yesterday's rollout?
Hector M: Yep. We rolled the new origin-proxy that coalesces pings to reduce egress. It might be batching pongs or delaying them under load. Browsers expect timely pongs (or they show spinner), while our control plane only watches TCP state.
Yvonne C: Can you paste a short trace (sanitized)? Need timing of ping/pong vs payload.
Tara V: snippet (sanitized):
```
> client -> edge: ping
> edge -> origin: batched_ping (held 120ms)
> origin -> edge: pong (batched)
> edge -> client: (no immediate pong)  -- UI shows spinner ~250ms
> data: {"delta":"..."}
```
Hector M: That 120-250ms jitter is what trips some SDKs' stall detectors. The console shows the socket OPEN because TCP didn't close. UX/alerts mismatch.
Yvonne C: Two problems: 1) telemetry granularity — console needs last-byte/last-pong time, not just open/closed. 2) routing/quotas — when coalescing pings we mask origin load spikes, making soft-throttle decisions inaccurate.
Tara V: UX request: add a "last-activity-ms" column to live sessions that can display last SSE/WS payload or pong arrival. Also a time-series tile for "ping->pong lag" per route so PMs can correlate to rollouts.
Hector M: Agree. Short-term experiment: revert coalescing on a tiny canary (us-east-2) and add verbose ping telemetry for 0.5% sessions to capture raw ping/pong timings. If stalls disappear, we know coalescing is culprit.
Yvonne C: Also propose a lightweight server header x-last-pong-ms for the response path so SDKs can decide not to declare stall if server indicates recent pong. Devex could add a tiny debounce in JS/py SDKs using that header.
Tara V: Good. Billing concern: are customers charged twice when clients retry on perceived stall? billing counts tokens when emitted, so dupes possible if SDKs re-send idempotent requests. We should add a header x-graceful-restart during any graceful restart to reduce retries.
diag-bot: quick-query: ping_pong_lag_mean(route=/v1/ws, last_1h) -> 85ms; ping_pong_90pct -> 240ms; fast_reconnect_rate -> 0.03%
Hector M: 90pct 240ms matches UI spinner window. So coalescing leads to bad tail latency for ping/pong. Action items: 1) infra: add ping->pong lag metric and sample raw timings; 2) infra: revert coalescing on canary us-east-2; 3) console: add last-activity-ms and ping-pong tile; 4) devex: SDK debounce honor x-last-pong-ms and x-graceful-restart headers.
Tara V: @deploy-bot can you queue rollback of ping-coalescing on canary us-east-2 and add verbose ping telemetry for 0.5%?
deploy-bot: Deploy job queued by Tara V: rollback/ping-coalescing -> canary us-east-2; telemetry/sample-ping-pong -> 0.5%. CI smoke queued. :white_check_mark:
Yvonne C: Long-term: routing layer should expose "probe-origin-lag" so throttler decisions can account for coalesced signal. Otherwise we under- or over-react to origin pressure.
Hector M: Also add console alert: ping_pong_90pct(route)>200ms && silent_pause_rate>0.2% => tag active rollout. That helps PMs correlate.
Tara V: I'll monitor the canary and collect a few example traces to attach to the new tile. Thanks team. Will post back in 30m with results. :thumbsup:
